# The Framework Integers {#sec-integers}

The four integers $\{3, 4, 7, 13\}$ are not inputs to FTD. They are outputs of the master quadratic and the Moore neighborhood geometry. This chapter derives each integer and establishes the relations among them.

## 10.1 The four integers [THEOREM]

From the roots of the master quadratic (@sec-roots) and the lattice geometry (@sec-moore):

| Integer | Symbol | Value | Derivation |
|---------|--------|-------|------------|
| Colors | $N_c$ | 3 | $\lfloor x_- \rfloor = \lfloor 3.024 \rfloor = 3$ |
| Base | $N_{\text{base}}$ | 4 | $|\text{Aut}(E_i)| = |\mathbb{Z}[i]^*| = 4$ |
| QCD beta | $b_3$ | 7 | $(11N_c - 2N_f)/3 = (33 - 12)/3 = 7$ |
| Effective DOF | $N_{\text{eff}}$ | 13 | $b_3 + 2N_c = 7 + 6 = 13$ |

Each derivation is detailed below.

## 10.2 $N_c = 3$: the number of colors [SELECTION]

From $x_- = 3.024$ and topological quantization of color charge: $N_c = \lfloor x_- \rfloor = 3$. This is the number of quark colors in QCD, the dimension of the fundamental representation of $SU(3)$, and the BCC flux-component count.

The fractional part $x_- - N_c = 0.024$ is interpreted as a confining correction: the running coupling at the confinement scale differs from the integer by approximately $\alpha_s(M_Z) / (4\pi) \approx 0.009$. [SELECTION]

## 10.3 $N_{\text{base}} = 4$: the base dimension [THEOREM]

The automorphism group of the CM curve $E_i: y^2 = x^3 - x$ is:
$$
\text{Aut}(E_i) = \{1, -1, i, -i\} \cong \mathbb{Z}_4
$$

This is the group of units of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$. Its order is $N_{\text{base}} = 4$. Equivalently:

- $N_{\text{base}} = \sqrt{K} = \sqrt{16} = 4$ (from the DOF coefficient)
- $N_{\text{base}} = D + 1 = 4$ (spatial dimensions plus time)
- $N_{\text{base}} = $ number of Hurwitz quaternion units modulo sign $= 4$

## 10.4 $b_3 = 7$: the QCD beta function coefficient [THEOREM]

The one-loop beta function coefficient of $SU(N_c)$ gauge theory with $N_f$ quark flavors is:
$$
b_0 = \frac{11N_c - 2N_f}{3}
$$

With $N_c = 3$ and $N_f = 6$ (the Standard Model has 6 quark flavors):
$$
b_3 = \frac{11 \times 3 - 2 \times 6}{3} = \frac{33 - 12}{3} = 7
$$

The value $N_f = 6$ is itself derivable: the Moore Layer Theorem gives 3 generations of quarks, each with 2 flavors (up-type and down-type), giving $N_f = 3 \times 2 = 6$. So $b_3 = 7$ is a consequence of $N_c = 3$ and the generation count. [THEOREM given $N_c = 3$ and $N_f = 6$]

## 10.5 $N_{\text{eff}} = 13$: effective degrees of freedom [THEOREM]

$$
N_{\text{eff}} = b_3 + 2N_c = 7 + 6 = 13
$$

$N_{\text{eff}}$ appears throughout the framework:

- **Strong coupling at $M_Z$:** $\alpha_s(M_Z) = b_3 / (b_3 + 4N_{\text{eff}}) = 7/59 = 0.1186$ (experimental: $0.1179 \pm 0.0009$)
- **Proton mass ratio:** $m_p/m_e = N_{\text{eff}}/\alpha + \ldots = 13 \times 137.036 + \ldots = 1836.47$
- **Moore eigenvalue:** 13 appears as a distinct eigenvalue of the $27 \times 27$ Moore adjacency matrix
- **Fibonacci:** $N_{\text{eff}} = F_7 = 13$ (the 7th Fibonacci number)

## 10.6 Relations among the integers [THEOREM]

The four integers satisfy:

$$
N_c + N_{\text{base}} + b_3 + N_{\text{eff}} = 3 + 4 + 7 + 13 = 27 = 3^3 = |N^M(v)|
\tag{10.1}
$$

$$
b_3 = N_c + N_{\text{base}} = 3 + 4 = 7
\tag{10.2}
$$

$$
N_{\text{eff}} = b_3 + 2N_c = N_c + N_{\text{base}} + 2N_c = 3N_c + N_{\text{base}} = 13
\tag{10.3}
$$

$$
N_{\text{base}}^2 = K = 16 \qquad (\text{DOF coefficient})
\tag{10.4}
$$

Relation (10.1) is numerically exact but its interpretation is [CONJECTURE]: the sum of the framework integers equals the Moore neighborhood size. Whether this reflects a deep partition of the 27 voxels into four functionally distinct subsets is an open question.

## 10.7 The Fibonacci connection [THEOREM for the arithmetic]

The sequence $3, 4, 7$ is Fibonacci-like: $3 + 4 = 7$. The next term, $7 + 6 = 13$, is the actual Fibonacci number $F_7$. The sequence continues: $7 + 13 = 20$, $13 + 20 = 33$, where 33 = $11 N_c$ (the numerator of $b_3$).

The Fibonacci connection is [CONJECTURE] --- it may reflect the recursive self-similar structure of the lattice dynamics or may be numerological coincidence. It is noted for completeness.
